clue.text: Scotsman in French battle represents 13 …

indicators.note: in places the Scotsman inside the name of the French battle

parts.note: the Marne was the site of two great First World War battles in France
Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A Scot who fought at a French battle stands as a symbol of feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is SENSIBILITY, and in Austen's Sense and Sensibility Marianne Dashwood embodies it; the trailing dots lead into the next clue, about her sister.
explanation.definitionFit: Marianne Dashwood is the heroine of Austen's novel who personifies emotional sensibility, set against her sensible sister.

clue.text: … her sister's flower is coming up gold

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the river's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, here the river Nile
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A woman's sister grows a golden flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is the crossword river, not a bloom: the NILE, read upwards, gives ELIN. The dots carry on from the previous clue, so 'her' is Marianne.
explanation.definitionFit: In Sense and Sensibility Elinor Dashwood is Marianne's elder sister, standing for sense.

clue.text: 2 5 acrosses or 2 chief 16s

definitions.meaning: two members of the Liverpool band of four, Lennon and McCartney, by their first names
two popes, the chief bishops, the twentieth-century pontiffs who bore both names

explanation.walkthrough: Here '2' is the number two, not a reference to 2-down; 5 across is BEATLE and 16 is BISHOP.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles' Lennon and McCartney had these first names, and two twentieth-century popes took this double papal name.

clue.text: Quick! The city's lost its North End

indicators.note: losing its North end means the city drops the N at its tail, N being North

parts.note: Preston is a city in Lancashire; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: Hurry: a city has lost its football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Preston North End is the city's football club, which makes 'North End' read naturally; here N (North) is cut from the end of PRESTON.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is the musical direction meaning very fast, and also a conjuror's exclamation of quickness.

clue.text: 1 of 4 live to expound the tale

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: to expound is to set something out afresh, so the letters of the tale are rearranged

explanation.surface: One of a group of four lives to tell the story.
explanation.definitionFit: John, Paul, George and Ringo made up the Fab Four, so a Beatle is one of four.

clue.text: Speaker to purchase mushrooms and mussel, say

indicators.note: a speaker voices the words, so the sound of the phrase is what counts

parts.note: to purchase is to buy, and ceps are edible mushrooms

explanation.surface: A speaker wants to buy mushrooms and a mussel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mussel, say' is itself a sound-alike: a mussel sounds like a muscle, and the biceps is an example of one.
explanation.definitionFit: The biceps is a muscle of the upper arm, and the clue spells muscle as the shellfish it sounds like.

clue.text: Dance to get right in the polls?

indicators.note: in signals that the letter for right goes inside the pollster's name

parts.note: MORI's are the polls of MORI, a British opinion-polling company

explanation.surface: A dance is staged to win the right result in the polls.
explanation.walkthrough: MORI was a well-known British market-research and polling firm; its polls, MORI'S, take R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Morris dancing is a traditional English folk dance performed with bells and sticks.

clue.text: Royal corpse is resurrected by Brown

indicators.note: resurrected means raised up, so in a down clue the pieces read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: 'Queen Anne's dead' is an old saying for stale news, so the dead royal is Anne

explanation.surface: A dead royal is brought back to life by someone called Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resurrected' turns ANNE IS upwards to give the colour; 'Brown' looks like a surname but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earth pigment, and burnt or raw sienna gives a shade of brown.

clue.text: Big film in which Spooner makes antelope utter vain boasts

indicators.note: Spooner swaps the opening sounds of two words, here those of the antelope and the boasting

parts.note: a bok is a South African antelope, as in springbok
to bluster is to talk loudly and boastfully

explanation.surface: In a big film, an antelope boasts emptily, as the Reverend Spooner might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spooner makes' signals the swap of opening sounds; the result is said rather than spelt, so the K of the antelope stands for the CK sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockbuster is a hugely successful, expensive film, named after a bomb able to flatten a city block.

clue.text: I enter London suburb in case of battle

indicators.note: the letter I goes into the suburb's name, entering it

parts.note: Acton is a district of west London

explanation.surface: Someone enters a London suburb ready for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: An action is a military engagement, a fight between armed forces.

clue.text: Painter welcomed when lost at sea?

definitions.text: Painter welcomed when lost at sea?

parts.words: Painter welcomed when lost at sea?
parts.note: a sailor adrift would welcome someone who sights the shore, a seer of land, which also names a Victorian painter

explanation.walkthrough: Split the name into two words and it describes the lookout who spots the coast; Sir Edwin Landseer painted animals and the lions in Trafalgar Square.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edwin Landseer was a Victorian animal painter, best known for The Monarch of the Glen.

clue.text: Profound love holding desire back? I'm amazed!

indicators.note: back means the whole assembled string is read in reverse
holding means the first words contain the desire

parts.note: profound means deep
a yen is a longing or desire
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in wonder at a deep love restraining desire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the whole run, DEYENEPO, round; '?' and 'I'm' frame the definition as an exclamation of wonder.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wide-eyed in astonishment is a natural image for being amazed or taken aback.

clue.text: Article about security amid aggregate from Comets (film)

parts.note: rock is an aggregate of minerals
amid means in the midst of, around
the is the definite article
c is short for circa, about
a lock gives security

explanation.surface: A piece about security among a crowd of comets, perhaps a film review.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Haley and His Comets had the 1950s hit, which also titled a 1956 film; the pieces run here in reverse of the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock Around the Clock was the hit by Bill Haley and His Comets and gave its name to a 1956 film.

clue.text: See 14
Blessedness and inanity, one novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are formed afresh

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Bliss and silliness together make up one book.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle BLESSEDNESS, INANITY and I (one) into the title; 'novel' signals the rearrangement and also names what the result is.
explanation.definitionFit: Sense and Sensibility is Jane Austen's 1811 novel about the Dashwood sisters.

clue.text: See 12
Encore for dance piece

parts.note: bis is the French call for an encore, used in English concert halls
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A second performance of a dance number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' is a chessman, not a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: The bishop is one of the chessmen, moving diagonally across the board.

clue.text: Most of economic problem comes when parliament isn't sitting

indicators.note: most of means the word is cut short, keeping only its greater part

parts.note: a recession is a period of economic decline

explanation.surface: A big economic slump arrives just as the MPs go on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is a break in which a legislature such as Parliament stops sitting.

clue.text: Five fish attached to a piggery — not a pretty sight

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
the ide is a freshwater fish
on means attached to
a sty is a pigsty

explanation.surface: Five fish are tied up beside a pigsty, which is an ugly scene.
explanation.walkthrough: A video nasty was a violent or horrific video film, a term made notorious in 1980s Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A video nasty is a gruesome horror film on video, certainly an ugly thing to watch.

clue.text: Leave no doubt that blame doesn't start

indicators.note: not starting means the first letter of the word for blame is removed

parts.note: to censure is to blame or criticise

explanation.surface: Make certain the fault doesn't get started.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure something is to make certain of it, leaving no doubt.

clue.text: Go back into tent with dairy product

indicators.note: into puts the reversed word inside the tent

parts.note: a yurt is a circular tent used by nomads in Central Asia

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Head back into the tent with milk produce.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogurt is a fermented milk food, one of the standard dairy products.

clue.text: See 11
Ring about examples returned with poison gas

indicators.note: about means the word for ring goes round the reversed examples

parts.note: to ring someone is to phone them

indicators.note: returned means the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: egs is short for examples, plural of eg

explanation.surface: A ring around some returned samples comes with a toxic gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Phosgene is a choking gas used as a chemical weapon in the First World War.

clue.text: Good way to get proof of the pudding from here?

definitions.text: proof of the pudding from here?

parts.note: an alley is a narrow way or lane

explanation.surface: A good path to the proof that the pudding is good.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on two senses: a galley is a ship's kitchen where the pudding comes from, and a galley proof is a printer's trial sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: A galley is both a ship's kitchen, where the pudding is made, and a printer's proof sheet.

clue.text: People initially are not one with children

indicators.note: initially means take just the first letter of People

parts.note: NT is a common abbreviation for not

explanation.surface: People are, at first, not ones with children.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother or father is someone who has children.

clue.text: 2s that keep up

definitions.meaning: a brace is a pair, two of something, as in a brace of pheasants

explanation.walkthrough: '2s' are pairs, the number two pluralised; braces in British English are what Americans call suspenders.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace means a couple, and braces are trouser supports worn over the shoulders.
